findings.title: 00-index.md says "Four values vary by package" but the templates carry five
locations: policy/00-index.md:7-9 — "Four values vary by package and are substituted at render time: the leading identity of a docstring, the vector notation, the admonition-title rule and the admitted `\mathbf` strings"
policy/docs-rubric.md:248 (RULE.DOC.ARGCOV) — "For this package the check is a {{instruments.check-docs.argcov_policy}} tier."
findings.description: 00-index.md enumerates exactly four render-time template slots (leading_identity, vectors, admonition_titles, mathbf_allowed) and states the count as "Four values". But policy/docs-rubric.md itself carries a fifth `{{...}}` placeholder, `{{instruments.check-docs.argcov_policy}}` (in RULE.DOC.ARGCOV), which src/CLI/Sync.jl's `slots()` populates through the exact same mechanism and the exact same generic `render()` engine (Sync.jl:46-56) as the other four — it is not a separate substitution path. A grep of policy/*.md for `\{\{[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+\}\}` turns up exactly five distinct keys. This is exactly the staleness pattern RULE.DOC.CURRENT itself names: "a summary that names only a subset of what the code now provides is stale even if every sentence is literally true." It also undersells the package's own configuration surface: ARCHITECTURE §5.5 calls argcov_policy out by name as "the sole configurable tier" in the whole rulebook, yet the rulebook's own index of what varies per package omits it.
findings.resolution_hint: Either add the argument-coverage check tier to 00-index.md's enumeration ("Five values vary by package...: ...and the check-docs argument-coverage tier"), or, if the index is deliberately scoped to notation/prose parameters only and argcov_policy is meant to be documented solely via ARCHITECTURE §5.5, say so explicitly in 00-index.md rather than stating an unqualified "Four".
